regime.summary: Policy rate held at 22.0% while CPI (29.24%) is above it and rising over three months; bills (21.43%) sit just under the policy rate, so cuts are priced but not made. Index is up 22% in a month and 44% in three, so entry is extended. Situation file says hold bills and set a trigger to return, so keep equity exposure modest and skip chasing.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 22.0%; last MPC decision 2023-10-30: hold (+0bp)
CPI YoY 29.24% for 2023-11 (published by 2023-12-03); three months earlier (2023-08) 27.39%
6M T-bill minus policy rate -0.57pp (market pricing cuts); CPI rising over 3 months (+1.8pp)
Lesson: hold bills, and set a trigger to return.

core.thesis: Fertilizer is the least extended sector on six months (0.2464) and EFERT pays a 17.6% dividend yield at a 6.4 P/E with EPS up 129% year on year. Yield roughly offsets the 21.43% bill alternative only partly, so size is small. Quality tilt is weak, not proven.

MARI trades at a 3.6 P/E with a 9.7% dividend yield and EPS up 50% year on year, with a 6m gain of 33% that is small beside the market's 58%. Low multiple limits what must go right; the mechanism is weak evidence only.
